title: A summing RecursiveTask

blocks.text: The page's Q1 walks through `SumTask extends RecursiveTask<Long>`:

items: **Base case**: if `end - start <= threshold`, sum the range sequentially.

Otherwise split at `mid = start + (end - start) / 2` and run the two halves **at the same time**, then return the two sums added. The page's way is to fork the left subtask, compute the right one in the current thread and join the left last.

blocks.text: Its edge cases add: use `long` for sums of large `int` arrays.
Write `SumTask(array, start, end, threshold, probe)`. It sums `array[start..end)`. In each base case, call `probe.leaf(start, end)` once with the leaf's range (the tests use it to see how you split).

The halves really run in parallel: the tests check that the two leaves of a split can be inside `probe.leaf` **at the same time**, in a pool of two workers. Summing both halves in the current thread one after the other, or joining the forked half before computing the other, runs them one at a time and fails that check.

cases.says: The task returns the sum of array[start..end).
Sums are kept in a long, so large int values do not overflow.
A range of exactly threshold elements is summed sequentially, without splitting.
A longer range is split at its midpoint until every leaf holds at most threshold elements.
One half is forked while the other is computed, so the two halves run at the same time.

concepts: compute() solves a range of at most threshold elements sequentially and otherwise splits it and runs the two halves at the same time.
Sums of large int arrays are kept in a long so they do not overflow.
